name: Algebraix
tagline: Patented 'data algebra' SPARQL server from Algebraix Data; the company pivoted to blockchain in 2018.
description: Algebraix Data Corp. was a US company, active from about 2009, that built data-management software on its own mathematical 'data algebra', patenting ways to store and optimise data as algebraic relations across multiple storage formats. By 2013-2014 it marketed a cloud-hosted, high-performance graph database under the SPARQL Server name for semantic web and RDF analytics, and published a book and white papers on data algebra. In 2017-2018 the company recast itself around an ad-permission blockchain token (Permission.io) and the database disappeared from its site; the old algebraix.io domain now serves unrelated spam. It is listed here only for completeness.
statusNote: Database product dropped when Algebraix pivoted to a blockchain advertising venture (Permission.io) around 2018; no longer available.

scale.notes: No verifiable public information on production scale.

strengths: Distinctive mathematical (data algebra) approach to query optimisation, documented in patents
Positioned for SPARQL analytics in the cloud before managed RDF services were common
weaknesses: Product discontinued; no downloads, documentation or support
Little independent evidence of production deployments
Original domain now hosts unrelated content
useCases: Historical reference on algebraic approaches to data management
notIdealFor: Any current workload: the product is gone
